stem: A registrar is explaining to a parent that the temporary left-sided weakness after their child's seizure is a recognised post-seizure phenomenon. How long can this deficit last?
explanation: Todd's phenomenon can last minutes to hours. It is a transient post-seizure focal deficit rather than one that resolves only in seconds or persists for days.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 111

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because Todd's phenomenon can last longer than just a few seconds.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the deficit may persist beyond 5 minutes and can last for hours.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because Todd's phenomenon is a transient post-seizure weakness that can last minutes to hours.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because several days is not the typical duration described for Todd's phenomenon.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because persistence until the fever resolves is not the described time course.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
